name: Brunel University of London

settingEvidence.evidence: Brunel has everything on one campus in Uxbridge, west London

fees.text: £10,050 per year for Home (UK) students starting in 2027/28, subject to Parliamentary approval (Brunel's Economics course page). Brunel says the fee cap is expected to rise with inflation from 2028 onwards. Brunel has a separate page on placement-year fees and other course costs.

source.evidence: For the 2027/28 academic year, tuition fees for home students will be £10,050, subject to Parliamentary approval.

livingCosts.text: Undergraduate campus halls cost £179.97 to £381.78 a week in 2026/27: from a budget en-suite room (Mill) up to a large one-bed flat. Rooms cost £179.97 to £281.68 a week; studios and one-bed flats are £368.13 to £381.78. The undergraduate contract runs 13 September 2026 to 21 June 2027 (a budget en-suite totals £7,224.51).

source.evidence: Cost per week: £179.97

openDays.text: Next undergraduate open day: 21 November 2026, 9.30am-3.30pm on campus in Uxbridge (the 10 October 2026 open day has passed). No dates after that are published yet.

source.evidence: Get ready to explore your future at an Undergraduate Open Day on 10 October or 21 November 2026 from 9.30am - 3.30pm.

contextual.summary: Home-fee applicants who meet any one of Brunel's contextual criteria are eligible for a reduced contextual offer (published on each course page), but an offer is not guaranteed.
contextual.typicalReduction: One grade lower at A level on the courses recorded here (ABB standard, BBB contextual), as published on each course page.

criteria.detail: Applicants from areas of low higher education participation (POLAR4 Quintiles 1 and 2), worked out from your Home postcode and flagged automatically on your application.
Applicants who receive or are eligible to receive Free School Meals (asked on the UCAS application; Brunel can sometimes access Free School Meal data provided by UCAS).
Care-experienced applicants / care leavers (asked on the UCAS application).
Young carer aged 25 or under at enrolment, with a dependent family member or friend (asked on the UCAS application under 'Caring responsibilities').
People estranged from their parents or carers (under 25 at enrolment): no contact with your parents or legal guardians because of a permanent breakdown in the relationship.
Refugees, people granted Humanitarian Protection, and asylum seekers (confirm your residency status on the UCAS application; evidence is requested later).
Students who attended the Brunel Urban Scholars programme (a Saturday programme for school pupils).

Also on the list: applicants with a disability; mature applicants (21 or over on 1 September of the year the course starts); people from Gypsy, Roma and Traveller communities; applicants from UK Armed Forces families (Service Children) and applicants who have served in the UK Armed Forces.

contextual.rulesText: You would be considered a contextual applicant if you meet one or more of the criteria. Contextual admissions only applies to applicants eligible for Home fees and does not guarantee an offer for your preferred course. Contextual offers are published alongside the standard offer on course pages. Essential criteria like subject requirements cannot normally be waived, and Brunel may ask for verification.

notes: Brunel's course pages show 2026/27 entry requirements only (checked 2026-10-21), while the Home fee shown is already for 2027/28. All courses therefore use entry year 2026 (ABB, contextual BBB).
Brunel is not on UAT-UK's official TMUA list for 2027 entry, and none of these course pages mention an admissions test.

The Economics-related degrees are taught in Brunel Business School's Economics, Finance and Accounting department. Each course page also points to the 'Economics and Mathematics with an Integrated Foundation Year' course for foundation-year progression requirements; it is not recorded as a separate course.

Widening Access Travel Fund: home students from state schools who live outside the M25 and meet at least one widening access criterion may be able to claim travel costs for open days, offer holder days and interview/selection days (Brunel open days page).

Business and Management is the only course here that says it needs no A-level maths for its numerical content; the others list no A-level subject requirements either, only GCSE Mathematics at grade B/5 (grade C/4 for Business and Management).
